alert.title: Model is underforecasting commercial truck tires — fleet age distribution data is 5 months stale
alert.desc: The forecasting model for commercial truck tire SKUs uses fleet age distribution data to predict replacement cycle timing. That data has not been refreshed in 5 months and no longer reflects the current fleet composition — an aging fleet is driving higher near-term replacement demand than the model anticipates. Forecast bias has worsened for 3 straight cycles. The fix requires a model retrain with refreshed fleet age data, not a one-off override.

rca.finding: The model is underforecasting commercial truck tires because fleet age distribution data has not been refreshed in 5 months. All data pipelines are healthy — direct B2B and distributor feeds are current with no failures. The problem is the fleet age distribution input that drives replacement cycle timing predictions: its drift score is 0.78 against a 0.50 threshold, reflecting 5 months of fleet aging without a data refresh. As the truck fleet ages, near-term replacement demand increases — but the model is forecasting against a 5-month-old baseline. Bias has worsened every cycle for 3 straight cycles (+0.13 → +0.19 → +0.24). A prior incident 18 months ago had the same driver — a retrain with refreshed fleet data improved wMAPE by 1.9 points within 2 cycles.
